newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly has passed a motion to end monitoring in Romania following the Balkan country's recent democratic progress and the peaceful transition of power after last November's polls.
The decision is very important for Romania as it places the country on equal footing with other Central European countries expected to be invited to join NATO later this year.
* The Romanian parliament issued an appeal to parliaments of all NATO member-countries and to the alliance's leadership to support the country in its bid to win early NATO membership.

The appeal lists the country's arguments for NATO admission, including good relations with its neighbours, stability, civilian control over the army and the ability to enhance regional security and stability.
The text evokes Romania's participation in peacekeeping missions in Angola, Bosnia and Albania.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will participate in a meeting of NATO ambassadors in Brussels on Monday, accompanied by representatives of the foreign and defence ministries.

* The lower house of parliament, the Chamber of Deputies, adopted a report on the activity of the National Securities Commission (CNVM) since its inception. The report said the CNVM authorised 104 securities broker companies and 15 unit trusts.

* Regular meetings of the ruling coalition leaders with President Emil Constantinescu focus on the impact of government reform measures and have nothing to do with alleged tensions inside the coalition, Petre Roman, leader of the coalition member Democratic Party, told a press conference.
* Constantinescu is expected to meet leaders of the ruling coalition at Cotroceni in the evening to discuss reform and solutions for debts between companies. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 312 02 64
